Aeschylus in Philoctetes (fr. 250): 'but the Ionians [call them] attelaboi [locusts].'

And the cricket-like creatures are so called. The word is not known from elsewhere, written without accent in Hesychius and Photius. But the oxytone form in Hesychius is ἀκορνοί [locusts]: ἀττέλεβοι [locusts]. A similar form is κόρνοψ [a kind of locust].

I am on this rugged land.

ὀκρίδα [jagged], which the accent shows to be a substantive, Aeschylus used adjectivally for ὀκριόεσσαν [rugged], which he used at v. 282: ὀκριοέσσῃ χθονί τῇδε πελῶ [I am on this rugged land]. Therefore the scholiast correctly interpreted it as τραχεῖαν [rough], i.e. rough, rugged, just as grammarians explain ὀκριάζειν [to be rough] and ὀκριοῦσθαι [to be made rough] by τραχύνεσθαι [to be made rough], and Festus p. 181, 17 ed. Muell. taught that the ancient Latins called a rugged mountain 'ocrem', using examples from Livius Andronicus. The substantive ὄκρις [jagged point] they noted
a jagged (Aldus and Robortellus: akrida) ravine.
